cards.explanation: The answer is True. The father says, “Keep my commandments and live…” (Proverbs 7:2). Living and keeping his words go hand in hand. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friends, so trust me, I know the difference between sitting around and really living.

The answer is on his fingers and his heart. The father says, “Tie them to your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.” (Proverbs 7:3). One is right out front where his hands can see it, and the other goes deep inside. It's like a string tied on your finger so you don't forget, friends, except this one gets written on the heart too.

The answer is adulteress. The father wants wisdom and understanding close “…that they may keep you from the adulteress, from the stranger with seductive words.” (Proverbs 7:5). Notice the plan, friends. He doesn't just say stay away. He says to keep wisdom close like family so she keeps you away.

The answer is judgment. The father sees “…a young man lacking judgment…” (Proverbs 7:7). He says it right as he's picking him out from among the simple and the youths. I think he's saying the young man's problem isn't speed or strength, friends. It's that his good sense isn't switched on.

The answer is at twilight as day fades to dark. The verse says it's “…at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.” (Proverbs 7:9). The light is going out while he walks. I think the father wants us to notice, friends, how dim it's getting on this road.

The answer is False. The father says, “She is loud and defiant; her feet do not remain at home.” (Proverbs 7:11). So she's loud and defiant, friends, and home isn't where she stays. It's the opposite of quiet and settled.

The answer is True. She says, “…I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.” (Proverbs 7:15). She makes it sound like he's the one she's been looking for. It's the kind of line that makes you feel special for about three seconds, friends. Remember that the father calls her words seductive (Proverbs 7:5).

The answer is False. She says, “For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.” (Proverbs 7:19). She's telling the young man her husband is away, friends. Next verse she says how long he'll be gone.

The answer is not till the moon is full. She says her husband “…took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.” (Proverbs 7:20). That's the timing she gives, friends. She also says he's on a long journey (Proverbs 7:19), and she's telling this to the young man at twilight (Proverbs 7:9).

The answer is lips. The verse says, “With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.” (Proverbs 7:21). It's her words doing the work, friends. No tricks needed when the talking is that smooth.

The answer is that he doesn't see what's coming. The father says the young man follows her “on impulse” and ends up “…not knowing it will cost him his life.” (Proverbs 7:22-23). An ox heading to the slaughter and a deer bounding into a trap both walk right toward what's about to hurt them. I think the father wants us to feel how heavy that is, friends.

The answer is don't let your heart turn aside to her ways. The father says, “Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.” (Proverbs 7:25). He talks about the heart and about the paths in the same breath, friends. I think that's worth hanging onto.

The answer is False. The father says, “For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.” (Proverbs 7:26). He says it in two ways, friends: many, and many in number. It's a heavy line.

The answer is down to the chambers of death. The father says, “Her house is the road to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.” (Proverbs 7:27). Sheol is the place of the dead, friends. The road goes down, not up, which is how he closes the warning.
